prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1398; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact collision at an intersection involving the insured vehicle. The claimant reports being the driver of the vehicle struck on the passenger side and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the driver involved is listed as a named driver on the policy, with coverage in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the initial report, including the signal phase and direction of travel. The account has not changed across contacts.

Entry 4: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene and records the same sequence of events. Two independent witnesses were interviewed and their statements match the other driver's account and the scene photos.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle and reviewed the photos. The damage is concentrated along the driver's side door and quarter panel and is largely consistent with the angle and force described. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from records or the claimant.

Entry 6: The claimant reported a wrist fracture from bracing during impact. The injury is consistent with the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and no prior injury to the same area is known from the claimant's history or medical records requested so far.

Entry 7: Medical records show treatment followed a typical course, including immobilization, follow-up imaging, and physical therapy. Treatment frequency has tapered as the claimant's condition improved, in line with expected recovery.

Entry 8: Confirmed with the claimant's treating provider that the treatment plan and visit pattern are standard for this injury. No indication of unrelated or delayed care was found in the records reviewed.

Entry 9: Reviewed all information gathered to date. Witnesses, photos, the police report, and the other driver's statement support the reported sequence of events, and the injury and vehicle damage align with the described collision. File to continue with standard handling pending final medical updates.
